adopted: B1. THE EPISTEMIC STANDARD: 'It can verify that I put it there. Those are different claims.' Adopt verbatim as the standing law for every in-system test, audit, and validation readout in the mandala/star-system. Membership != validity, stated on the surface.
B2. Red-scar convention: failed marks persist in the alarm color (#C1121F), named, not hidden. Adopt for Gaven's anomaly display and health graphs — failures stay visible as scars with reasons.
B3. Ledger pattern: timestamped refusal/failure entries, capped (200), expandable panel, exposed via window.Witness.ledger(). This is the concrete shape for the Evidence Ledger's health entries.
B4. 'Audit the auditor': window.Witness exposes audit() itself so the test can be re-run by anyone. Adopt as component standard alongside the honest API.
B5. META-LAW — a test that cannot fail is a painting, not a test. Every audit, validation, or proof we ship must have a reachable failure path, or it is decoration. Add to builder standard.

rejected: R1. The circular audit implementation: drawing from the pool then testing membership in the same pool. Rejected as an implementation — a test that cannot fail is decoration (see B5). Keep the honesty convention, discard the code pattern.
R2. The decorative gate: a CSS div labeled 'single gate' that gates nothing. Same rejection as the carrier import.
R3. Numerology-as-decision ('60 glyphs = 60 seconds in a minute'): constants need technical reasons, not poetic ones. Stating an aesthetic choice honestly is fine; dressing it as meaningful is not.
R4. The glyph lists as language data: hand-curated strings are not a language model of any kind. Do not cite these as language content; they are paint.

right_about: The audit-as-surface concept: a painting whose surface is the audit, blind spots stated aloud and rotating. Genuinely good — matches Nathan's 'every sensor is a claim' and the loud-stub standard.

The membership-vs-validity distinction, stated plainly: 'It can verify that I put it there. Those are different claims.' The single most valuable sentence in either file — this becomes a standing law.
Red scars: failed marks stay and turn #C1121F, named in the palette's own alarm color. Failure as persistent, labeled presence — not hidden, not retried silently.
Ledger discipline: every refusal logged with timestamp, glyph, claimed language, reason; capped, expandable, API-exposed. A real audit-trail shape.
'Failing paths printed in the same font as passing paths' — the borrowed law, correctly applied. No external calls, no CDN, seeded RNG with stated seed, honest failure path.
wrong_about: THE CORE FINDING: the audit is circular and cannot fail by construction. pickGlyph() draws only from POOL, which is built from the same LANGUAGES strings the audit tests membership against. The failure branch ('glyph not found in claimed language source') is unreachable for drawn glyphs; the 'language not in embedded source set' branch is unreachable too. The ledger will read 'No refusals yet' forever. The file confesses the audit is 'shallow' (blind spot b) but does not state the stronger truth: the test cannot fail. It is honest about the wrong thing. This is exactly why B5 becomes law.
The 'single gate' is a CSS div in the center of the screen labeled '515 Hz · single gate'. Glyphs are never passed through it; it gates nothing. Same decorative-gate overstatement as carrier.html.

'60 glyphs — 60 seconds in a minute; the field is a clock's worth of marks' and 'honest to a heartbeat' — numerology dressed as reasoning. The cadence is arbitrary; stating it as meaningful is the one dishonest note in an otherwise honest file.

The hand-curated glyph strings (e.g. Brainfuck '><+-.,[]') are real character sets but not parsed, compiled, or validity-tested — the file admits this, correctly. They are paint, not language data; treat them as such.

what_it_is: A 2D painting whose surface is its own audit: glyphs from 28 hand-curated language character sets arrive on a grid, each membership-tested against its claimed language's embedded string; passes stay faint-gold, failures persist as red scars in a timestamped ledger; blind spots rotate aloud; zero dependencies, no network.
